definition: The legal power that Congress grants to an agency through legislation. An agency can only do what Congress has authorized it to do; if a statute does not clearly grant an agency a particular power, courts will not assume the agency has it — especially when the power raises significant constitutional questions.
examples: The Supreme Court will decide whether 8 U.S.C. §1188(g)(2) — the H-2A statute — actually gives the DOL the legal authority to adjudicate monetary claims against employers, separate from the constitutional question.
